claim: The profile is a named configuration bundle that deliberately excludes the running instance's fields - which is the sourced boundary between this card and card 3.3.
query: SandboxBlueprint configuration shared between Sandbox SandboxTemplate excludes runtime-only fields operatingMode lifecycle
snippet:
SandboxBlueprint defines the configuration shared between Sandbox and SandboxTemplate.
It deliberately excludes runtime-only fields (operatingMode, lifecycle).
title: API Reference | Agent Sandbox
topic: What a runtime profile is, and what it deliberately leaves out

claim: A profile's unstated field is not undefined: the controller closes it, which is the only secure-by-default rule sourced anywhere in this batch.
query: SandboxTemplate AutomountServiceAccountToken not specified controller defaults false secure-by-default environment
snippet:
podTemplate describes the pod that will be created in the sandbox.
Note: When provisioned via a SandboxTemplate (such as by a SandboxClaim or SandboxWarmPool),
if AutomountServiceAccountToken is not specified in the PodSpec, the controller defaults it
to false to ensure a secure-by-default environment.
title: API Reference | Agent Sandbox
topic: The secure-by-default rule a profile carries

claim: Profile list fields replace rather than merge, the same last-write-wins semantics card 6.3's facets have.
query: sandbox volumeClaimTemplates list is atomic updates replace entire list rather than merging
snippet: NOTE: This list is atomic. Updates to this field will replace the entire list rather than merging with existing entries.
title: API Reference | Agent Sandbox
topic: How a profile's list fields are updated

claim: A worked instance of the same concept, and it carries a cardinality rule the Kubernetes API does not: one policy per cluster.
query: CoreWeave sandbox policy fields managed runner cluster hosts at most one runner one policy governs one cluster
snippet: This page documents every field in a sandbox policy. A policy is carried on a managed runner as the policy field, and because a cluster hosts at most one runner, one policy governs one cluster.
title: Policy reference - CoreWeave Docs
topic: A profile as one implementation actually ships it

claim: Isolation here is explicitly relative rather than absolute, and is declared per direction - the value domain of the card's network half.
query: Kubernetes two sorts of isolation pod egress ingress connections established not absolute some restrictions apply
snippet:
There are two sorts of isolation for a pod: isolation for egress, and isolation for ingress.
They concern what connections may be established. "Isolation" here is not absolute, rather it
means "some restrictions apply".
title: Network Policies | Kubernetes
topic: The two directions isolation is declared in, and what isolation means

claim: Egress is wide open unless a policy says otherwise, which is the default a platform claiming declared egress must override.
query: Kubernetes by default pod non-isolated for egress all outbound connections allowed
snippet: By default, a pod is non-isolated for egress; all outbound connections are allowed.
title: Network Policies | Kubernetes

claim: Once isolated, the allow-list is the whole permission set - there is no implicit residue.
query: Kubernetes pod isolated for egress only allowed connections egress list NetworkPolicy applies
snippet:
When a pod is isolated for egress, the only allowed connections from the pod are those allowed by
the egress list of some NetworkPolicy that applies to the pod for egress.
title: Network Policies | Kubernetes
topic: What isolation actually permits once declared

claim: Policies union rather than intersect, so adding a policy can only widen what is permitted.
query: Kubernetes effects of egress lists combine additively
snippet: The effects of those egress lists combine additively.
title: Network Policies | Kubernetes
topic: How two policies on one pod combine

claim: Ingress has the same open default as egress, declared independently.
query: Kubernetes by default pod non-isolated for ingress all inbound connections allowed
snippet: By default, a pod is non-isolated for ingress; all inbound connections are allowed.
title: Network Policies | Kubernetes

claim: Enforcement is a separate component's job, stated as a requirement on the cluster rather than provided by the API.
query: Kubernetes cluster must use network plugin that supports NetworkPolicy enforcement
snippet: Your cluster must use a network plugin that supports NetworkPolicy enforcement.
title: Network Policies | Kubernetes
topic: What the policy needs to be more than a document

claim: A declared isolation policy with no controller behind it silently does nothing - the exact shape of defect this repo calls claimed rather than measured.
query: Kubernetes creating NetworkPolicy resource without controller that implements it will have no effect
snippet: Creating a NetworkPolicy resource without a controller that implements it will have no effect.
title: Network Policies | Kubernetes
topic: What a declared policy does when nothing enforces it

claim: The WASM option's isolation word is hermetic, and this source is a release announcement rather than a specification - see gaps.
query: WebAssembly Wasm components container format type system typed hermetic binaries libraries
snippet:
Wasm components are a container format and type
system that wrap Core Wasm instructions into typed, hermetic binaries and libraries (think: ELF).
title: Announcing WASI 0.2.1 | Bytecode Alliance
topic: The third runtime kind the card names
